# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

- [ ] Tests run and pass under `--project unit` (fast, no browser).

- Reference the launcher item's content-locator abstraction (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) for the dependency-injection pattern.

# Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine

External producer action (Steamworks partner backend). The achievement work for
Main Street (and the other TCE games) maps challenge completions to persistent
Steam achievements, but no Steamworks project/App ID exists yet — so the
matching achievement API names cannot be registered.

## Goal / user story

As the Tableau Card Engine producer, I need a Steamworks project (App ID) for
the game so that achievements can be registered and unlocked for real players.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Steamworks partner project exists for Tableau Card Engine and has an assigned App ID.
2. The App ID is recorded somewhere version-controlled (launcher config or documented env/config) so `steamworks.js` can initialise against it.
3. The producer account can access the project's achievement configuration in the Steamworks partner backend.

## Constraints

- Producer/external action — not implementable by a code agent.
- Must be completed before the achievement-registration item (see dependency below).

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ**: Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements (epic)
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7**: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (blocking consumer)

# Intake Brief: Platform-agnostic action unlocks — reward games and in-game DLC for arbitrary actions on any platform

## Problem statement

The launcher already unlocks a bundled game when the player follows on Steam, but the mechanism is Steam-shaped end to end (`FollowSource`, `SteamFollowService`, the single `bonusGameId`, `steamFollow:*` IPC). To grow the audience across storefronts we need to reward **arbitrary actions on any platform** — follow on Steam, follow on itch.io, review on WaveDash, wishlist, etc. — through **one config-driven, platform-agnostic unlock mechanism** with a **pluggable verification model**. The same mechanism must also unlock **DLC within an existing game** (extra content inside a game the player already has), not just whole bundled games.

## Users

- **Players on any storefront** — earn a bundled game, or extra content (DLC) inside a game they already have, for a light action (follow/review/wishlist) on whichever platform they use, not just Steam.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — add a new reward (game **or** DLC) by editing config and (if needed) adding a verifier, without touching the unlock service, persistence, IPC, or the lock model.
- **TCE game authors** — gate their own DLC content on the unified unlock state through one engine/client API, instead of rolling their own persistence or platform checks.

**User stories:**
- As an itch.io player, I want a bundled game to unlock in my launcher after I follow the TCE itch.io page, so I am rewarded on the platform I already use.
- As a player, I want a DLC pack for a game I already own to unlock after I complete the required action, so the reward is visible inside that game.
- As a publisher, I want to configure "action X on platform Y unlocks game Z" as data, so I can run new reward campaigns without a code change per platform where detection is not possible.
- As a publisher, I need the verification method per rule to be pluggable, so I can start with a manual self-attest and later upgrade specific platforms to API/OAuth detection without reworking the unlock flow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config-driven, platform-agnostic reward model.** A typed `UnlockRule` discriminated union — `trigger.kind: 'platform-action' | 'achievement'` and `target.kind: 'game' | 'dlc'` — plus a platform-action rule set live in `electron/unlock-rules.ts` (shared with the achievement give-aways); rules map `(platform, action) → target` and no game title, DLC id, platform name, action name, or URL is hard-coded in logic.
2. **Pluggable verification.** Action verification goes through an `ActionVerifier` interface resolved from config: the manual self-attest verifier is the default for platforms without a detection API, and Steam follow detection is wired as one verifier. Adding a new platform requires a new verifier and a config entry only — no change to the unlock service, store, or IPC.
3. **One non-Steam game reward works end-to-end.** An itch.io "follow" rule unlocks its designated game through the manual self-attest path, while the existing Steam follow reward (Feudalism) behaves unchanged and its existing tests still pass.
4. **DLC unlock targets work end-to-end.** The mechanism unlocks **in-game DLC as well as whole games**: a rule can target `{kind:'dlc', gameId, dlcId}`, unlock state is persisted per target and exposed to the renderer via a total read API, and at least one game (or Gym scene) gates a DLC content item on that state — the content is unreachable until the action is verified and reachable afterwards, with a documented locked-state presentation.
5. **Unified persistence and lock computation.** Unlocks persist through the unified `ContentUnlockStore` (shared with the achievement give-aways), keyed by target, survive relaunch, are idempotent, and both launcher lock computation (Game Selector) and in-game DLC checks consume the same state so locked/unlocked results are consistent.
6. **Graceful degradation and browser safety.** With no config, no resolving verifier, no Electron bridge, or Steam absent, the service is a total no-op (never throws, never fabricates an unlock); the plain-browser web build remains fully playable, and a DLC whose unlock state cannot be read degrades to "not unlocked" without crashing the owning game.
7. **Test coverage.** Deterministic unit tests cover rule evaluation (game and DLC targets), manual self-attest unlock, idempotent repeat, cross-launch persistence, missing-config/verifier degradation, the no-hard-coded-titles guarantee, and DLC gating on/off; they pass under `--project unit` (plus a browser/Gym test for the gated-content UI if applicable).
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — code comments, `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and the Steam/action-reward QA doc (config format, how to add a platform/action/verifier, how a game gates DLC on unlock state, the cross-repo model, and the self-attest honour-system caveat).
9. **Quality gate.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` succeeds.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't reinvent.** The unlock remains game-agnostic bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches — reusing `ContentUnlockStore`/`FileUnlockStore` from the existing Steam follow mechanism (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC) and the unified store contract (CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G).
- **Architecture decision (producer, option a).** One unified, discriminated `UnlockRule` trigger model shared by platform-action rewards and achievement give-aways — a single source of truth for the Game Selector, not two parallel rule engines.
- **Verification decision (producer, option a).** Manual self-attest is the default for platforms with no detection API, but verification must be **pluggable** so specific platforms can later be upgraded to API/OAuth detection without touching the unlock flow.
- **Scope decision (producer, option a).** This item generalises the mechanism and ships **Steam (existing) plus one non-Steam proof-of-generality (itch.io follow)**. WaveDash review and further platforms are explicitly out of scope here and are recorded as follow-up work items.
- **DLC scope addition (producer).** The mechanism must also unlock **DLC within existing games**, not just whole games. The `target` is therefore a discriminated union (`game` | `dlc`); DLC content delivery already has a foundation in `electron/content-locator.ts` (Steam DLC content directory), which this item does not replace — it adds the *unlock* gate around it.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** The launcher/engine owns the unlock mechanism, persistence, config, and the read API; each game owns its DLC content and its gating call site. At least one game or Gym scene must prove the gate end-to-end; per-game gating for the full catalogue is follow-up work.
- **Renderer never imports an SDK.** The main process owns the only concrete sources/verifiers; the context bridge stays narrow and **total** (every handler returns a safe value, never throws).
- **Backward compatibility.** The existing `window.tce.steamFollow` surface and follow-unlock behaviour remain working until (and if) callers migrate to the generalised surface.
- **Config is data; credentials are never committed.** Platform URLs/identifiers are config; secrets stay in env/gitignored local files.
- **Licensing.** All code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates.** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before review.

## Existing state

- `electron/steam-follow.ts` — `FollowSource` interface, `SteamFollowService`, `UnlockStore`/`MemoryUnlockStore`/`FileUnlockStore`, single `bonusGameId`, `claimManually()` self-attest fallback.
- `electron/steam-follow-steamworks.ts` + `electron/steam-follow-native.ts` + `native/steam-friends` — real Steam detection with capability-ordered fallback.
- `electron/steam-follow-ipc.ts` — `STEAM_FOLLOW_CHANNELS` + pure handler table; `electron/preload.cjs` exposes `window.tce.steamFollow`.
- `electron/bonus-catalog.json` — config-driven catalog, `bonusGameId: feudalism`; `resolveBonusGame()` resolves it.
- `src/ui/steam-lock.ts` — pure `computeSteamLocks`/`applySteamLocks` (`STEAM_LOCK_FOLLOW`, `STEAM_LOCK_MILESTONE`, `STEAM_LOCK_UNAVAILABLE`).
- `src/ui/steam-follow-client.ts` — typed renderer client with graceful browser fallback.
- `electron/content-locator.ts` + `electron/launcher-config.ts` — existing Steam DLC content-directory resolution (`ContentDirectoryProvider`), i.e. how DLC *content* is located today (not how it is gated).
- Tests under `tests/steam-follow/`.

## Desired change

1. Introduce a unified, discriminated reward model — `UnlockRule` (`trigger.kind: 'platform-action' | 'achievement'`) and `UnlockRuleSet` — in a shared module (`electron/unlock-rules.ts`), with a pure evaluator and deterministic fakes (test-first).
2. Define an `ActionVerifier` seam and resolve verifiers from config; implement the **manual self-attest** verifier as the default and adapt the existing **Steam** follow source as one verifier.
3. Generalise the service (rename/refactor `SteamFollowService` → a platform-agnostic `ActionRewardService`) to evaluate all platform-action rules against the unified store, and keep the Steam follow rule working through the same path.
4. Generalise persistence to the unified `ContentUnlockStore` keyed by target, and generalise the lock computation (`steam-lock.ts` → action-reward-aware) so the Game Selector reads one source of truth.
5. Add config for an itch.io follow reward plus the designated game, wire a generalised IPC/preload surface (keeping `steamFollow` backward compatible), and expose a total read API (`isUnlocked(target)` / `getUnlocks()`) over the bridge.
6. Add in-game DLC support: a pure engine/client helper that gates content on `isUnlocked({kind:'dlc', gameId, dlcId})`, plus one proof — a Gym scene and/or one `tce-<game>` DLC content item that is only reachable after the action is verified.
7. Add unit tests for the contract (game + DLC targets), the service, the verifiers, DLC gating, and degradation paths; update docs (including the cross-repo gating guide).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `electron/unlock-rules.ts` — **new**: `UnlockRule`/`UnlockRuleSet` types, pure rule evaluation, no hard-coded titles/platforms/actions.
- `electron/action-verifiers.ts` — **new**: `ActionVerifier` interface, manual self-attest verifier, verifier registry/resolution.
- `electron/action-rewards.ts` / `electron/action-rewards-service.ts` — **new (or generalised from `steam-follow.ts`)**: platform-agnostic service over the unified store.
- `electron/action-rewards.json` — **new**: config mapping platform actions to target games (itch.io follow minimum).
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` — refactor: unlock service becomes one `ActionRewardService` path; keep `FollowSource` and self-attest.
- `electron/steam-follow-ipc.ts` — generalise channels / add action-reward channels (keep `steamFollow:*` compatible).
- `electron/preload.cjs` — expose the generalised bridge (additive).
- `electron/bonus-catalog.json` — extend with the itch.io-gated game entry.
- `src/ui/steam-lock.ts` — generalise lock computation to consume follow + action-reward status (games and DLC).
- `src/ui/steam-follow-client.ts` → generalised client (additive; keep Steam methods).
- `src/ui/content-unlock-client.ts` — **new**: total read API over the bridge (`isUnlocked(target)`, `getUnlocks()`), browser fallback returns "not unlocked".
- `src/core-engine/DlcGate.ts` (or similar) — **new**: pure, framework-free helper a game uses to gate DLC content on the unlock state.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymDlcUnlockScene.ts` — **new (proof)**: Gym scene showing DLC content gated by the unified unlock state.
- `../tce-<game>/src/**` — **cross-repo (proof, optional)**: one game gates a DLC content item on the unlock state (recorded on this core item if the game repo has no Worklog store).
- `electron/content-locator.ts` — unchanged in responsibility; referenced as the existing DLC content-delivery foundation.
- `tests/platform-action-rewards/*.test.ts` — **new**: contract (game + DLC), service, verifier, gating, degradation, persistence tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md` — document the config format, adding a platform/verifier, the DLC gating API + cross-repo model, and the self-attest caveat.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC** — Follow-on-Steam incentive (the mechanism being generalised). *Related / superseded-in-shape by this item.*
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL** — Achievement give-aways epic (co-owns the unified `ContentUnlockStore` and the `UnlockRule` model).
- **CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G** — Give-away unlock contract + deterministic fakes (unified multi-game `ContentUnlockStore`); this item's unified `UnlockRule` must not diverge from it.
- **CG-0MUNW66DO004N7V6** — Game Selector locked state and unlock-progress UI (consumes the lock computation produced here).
- **CG-0MUNW670D000V1MV** — Give-away config/catalog extension + drift validator (config conventions to align with).
- **CG-0MUOC5OV4006OTLG**, **CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1** — Steam follow detection E2E / native addon.
- Docs: `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md`, `docs/dev/steam-follow-native-spike.md`, `AGENTS.md` §20 (optional native integrations behind an interface).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Coordination risk:** the unified `UnlockRule` model overlaps the achievement give-away contract (CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G) and the selector UI (CG-0MUNW66DO004N7V6). *Mitigation:* this item defines the shared model and lock computation; the other items consume it. Record the relationship before implementation.
- **Honour-system risk:** manual self-attest is trivially bypassable. *Mitigation:* accepted by producer decision (option a); verification is pluggable so platforms can be upgraded; the caveat is documented in the QA doc.
- **No-detection-API risk:** itch.io/WaveDash expose no follow/review detection. *Mitigation:* do not promise detection; default to self-attest after opening the action URL.
- **Backward-compatibility risk:** generalising `steamFollow` could break the existing follow UI/tests. *Mitigation:* keep `steamFollow:*` and `window.tce.steamFollow` working; make the new surface additive; existing follow tests must still pass.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "any platform" invites unbounded adapter work. *Mitigation:* option (a) scope — ship Steam + itch.io proof-of-generality only; capture further platforms as linked follow-up work items.
- **Assumption:** the itch.io "follow" action is a plain link-out with no auth; the self-attest unlock persists exactly like an automatic unlock.
- **DLC gating / cross-repo risk:** gating DLC inside games spans the core repo (mechanism, read API) and one or more `tce-<game>` repos (content + call site), and the DLC content-delivery model already exists (`content-locator.ts`) — wiring the gate must not disturb the load path. *Mitigation:* keep the gate a pure read-only check layered over the existing content locator; prove it in one place (Gym scene and/or one game) and capture per-game roll-out as follow-ups.
- **Assumption:** the itch.io "follow" action is a plain link-out with no auth; the self-attest unlock persists exactly like an automatic unlock.
- **Assumption:** the unified `ContentUnlockStore` (CG-0MUNW63UL0086J3G) is available for reuse, or is co-developed with this item as the lead contract, and can be keyed by target (`game` or `dlc`).
- **Assumption:** a DLC target is identified by `(gameId, dlcId)`, with `dlcId` owned by the game repo's content definition (no central DLC registry is introduced by this item).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope of platform adapters):** "Build Steam + itch.io follow + WaveDash review adapters all in this item, or generalise the mechanism and ship Steam plus one non-Steam proof-of-generality?" — **Answer (producer): option (a)** — generalise the mechanism and ship Steam plus one non-Steam proof-of-generality (itch.io follow); further platforms recorded as follow-ups. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (verification model):** "How are actions verified on platforms with no public detection API — manual self-attest, OAuth/API where available, or proof submission?" — **Answer (producer): option (a) for now, and validation should be pluggable** — manual self-attest is the default, behind a pluggable verifier seam so platforms can later be upgraded. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (architecture):** "Unify platform-action rewards and achievement give-aways under one discriminated `UnlockRule` trigger model, or keep them as siblings over the same store?" — **Answer (producer): option (a)** — one unified trigger model and a single Game Selector source of truth. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 (DLC targets):** "Should the same mechanism also unlock DLC within existing games, not just whole games?" — **Answer (producer):** "Add the ability to unlock DLC within existing games using this mechanism as well." — the `target` is a discriminated union (`game` | `dlc`); DLC gating is in scope, leveraging the existing `content-locator` DLC content model. # Docs-consistency guard test for the "creating a new game" guide

Discovered-from: CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S. Test-first guard for the canonical
end-to-end new-game guide consolidation. This item defines the contract that
F2 (guide) and F4 (skill) must satisfy.

## Goal

As a docs maintainer, I want a fast filesystem-only unit test that pins the
guide's required lifecycle sections, resolves every relative link and in-file
anchor, and rejects the retired monorepo phrases — so the guide and skill
cannot silently drift again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test exists at `tests/tooling/creating-a-new-game-guide.test.ts` and runs under `--project unit` (the `unit` project includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`).
- [ ] The test asserts `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` exists and contains a heading for each required lifecycle section (the constant list defined in this item).
- [ ] The test asserts every relative Markdown link and every in-file anchor in the guide resolves to an existing file/anchor.
- [ ] The test asserts that neither the guide nor `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` contains the retired phrases ("add to the `GAMES` array" / `main.ts` `GAMES` catalogue instruction).
- [ ] The test performs no network access and no filesystem writes.
- [ ] The test is red before F2/F4 land and green after them (TDD evidence recorded on this item).

## Required lifecycle-section constant (children anchor to this)

The required-section list the test pins:

1. Concept and ideation (`docs/the-build/`)
2. Intake and planning
3. Repository scaffold and multi-repo setup
4. Architecture and implementation
5. Testing profiles
6. CI and release
7. Game registration (`GAME_INFO` + `configs/*.json` presets)
8. Assets and licensing
9. Documentation update
10. Publication

## Minimal implementation

- `node:fs` / `node:path` reads only; a regex link/anchor extractor; a constant required-section list.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/tooling/creating-a-new-game-guide.test.ts` — **new**.
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — asserted target (created by F2).
- `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` — asserted target (slimmed by F4).

## Dependencies

- None (first item, test-first ordering).
